statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. CME equity-index futures remain halted since the Friday settle, so no Nasdaq-100 price path exists in any hour of this horizon and Tail is held at a closed-venue floor while Stress moves into the elevated band on a verified Saturday US-Iran escalation.
recommendation: Tail holds a closed-venue floor of 4-5% across all 24 published hours, so the deterministic mapping stays EA_ON and green throughout. Stress starts at 48% and drifts to 55%, inside the elevated band for the whole horizon, reflecting Saturday's verified US-Iran exchange, a hawkish September rate path, an impaired Strait of Hormuz and a data-heavy week containing August PPI on 10 September and August CPI on 11 September. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: Nasdaq-100 unquoted at 29,544.15 through the CME weekend halt while a fresh US-Iran exchange - Iranian ballistic missiles at two US Navy ships answered by the destruction of three Iranian tankers - accumulates unpriced alongside a hawkish September rate path and a Strait of Hormuz energy premium
body: The Nasdaq-100 closed the August payroll session on Friday 4 September at 29,544.15, up 61.85 points or 0.21% from a 29,482.30 previous close, having ranged between 29,440.15 and 29,655.22. Price retraced repeatedly in both directions during that session, which is the opposite of the persistent no-retracement structure the Tail score measures. The material new development since the previous assessment is geopolitical rather than financial: NBC News and CBS News report that Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps launched multiple ballistic missiles at a US aircraft carrier and a guided-missile destroyer on Saturday morning US time, that both vessels evaded and no US personnel were harmed, and that US forces retaliated by permanently disabling three Iranian crude tankers - M/T Downy off Kharg Island, M/T Stark 1 near Jask and M/T Kylo in the Gulf of Oman - after their crews were evacuated. CENTCOM framed the response in explicitly economic terms. No strike on Iranian energy infrastructure has been verified, and the US President described the conflict as small potatoes while the Vice President declined to call it a war, so the exchange currently reads as a contained tit-for-tat inside a six-month conflict rather than a discontinuity. It nevertheless lands entirely unpriced, because CME equity-index futures have been halted since the 21:00 UTC Friday settle and are scheduled to reopen at 22:00 UTC on Sunday 6 September, roughly eight hours after the last hour published here. The energy channel remains the transmission path to watch: WTI settled at $91.48 after a weekly advance near 10% and Brent at $96.28 after 7.6%, Lloyd's List Intelligence counts 102 Strait of Hormuz transits last week against more than 130 a day before the conflict, and US retail diesel set a record $5.85 per gallon with regular gasoline at $4.15, the highest ever for a Labor Day weekend. Rates are the second unresolved input: Reuters reports August nonfarm payrolls up 162,000 against a consensus near 56,000 with unemployment unchanged at 4.1%, lifting the priced probability of a quarter-point increase at the 15-16 September FOMC to 58.4% from 49.4%, while the latest Federal Reserve H.15 observation carries the two-year at 4.34% and the ten-year at 4.77% after the ten-year touched 4.818% mid-week. The VIX settled at 14.53, up 1.47%, far below any level associated with disorderly repricing. Friday's internals were split rather than aligned: semiconductors were broadly higher while five of eight megacaps fell, with Tesla down 5.92% and Apple down 2.51%, and the S&P 500 and Dow both closed lower. That is an internally mixed signature, not the aligned cross-asset stack a genuine tail regime requires. Because no forecast hour in this assessment can contain an observable price path, Tail is scored at a closed-venue floor throughout rather than from any directional view, and the whole of the accumulating weight - hawkish September rate pricing, an energy-supply premium, an unresolved military exchange with an open weekend headline window, and a data-heavy week containing August PPI on 10 September and August CPI on 11 September - is carried by Stress, which sits in the elevated band across the horizon. The first genuine price-path evaluation of the new week belongs to a later assessment run after the Globex restart.

lookbackSummary: The preceding 24 hours cover the closing six hours of the August payroll session and the first eighteen hours of the CME weekend halt. The 15:00 UTC hour on 4 September was already past the release peak at Tail 17% and Stress 56% under a mixed mode, and every slot in this window maps to EA_ON and green. Tail decayed steadily through the remainder of the US cash session as the index retraced its highs and recovered, reaching Tail 12% and Stress 48% by 20:00 UTC with semiconductor leadership diverging from a softer broad tape. From the 21:00 UTC futures settlement onward every hour has been scored at the closed-venue floor of Tail 5% with mode normal, while Stress eased to 38% and then drifted back to 42% by 14:00 UTC as the unpriced weekend stack accumulated. All 24 slots carry a published Claude assessment.
outlookSummary: The entire 24-hour horizon falls inside the CME weekend halt, so no observable Nasdaq-100 price path can form in any published hour and the mapped policy state stays EA_ON throughout. Tail is held at a 4-5% closed-venue floor, easing to 4% through the dormant middle of the weekend and returning to 5% as the horizon tracks back toward the venue timeline. Stress opens at 48% and drifts to a 55% peak, inside the elevated band for the whole horizon, reflecting Saturday's verified US-Iran exchange, hawkish September rate pricing after the payroll beat, an energy premium from continued Strait of Hormuz disruption, and an open two-sided headline window that would express in a single reopening auction. Mode is characterised as normal through the dormant hours and mixed from 08:00 UTC on 6 September, where the accumulated stack is genuinely two-sided. Confidence eases from 86% to 79% purely through the ageing of Friday-anchored levels and Saturday reporting, staying inside the high band because coverage is complete. The horizon ends at 14:00 UTC on 6 September, roughly eight hours before the scheduled 22:00 UTC Globex restart, so the reopening auction and any gap it produces belong to a later assessment run.
